summary: This text is from a Retail Weather Insurance Policy issued by TATA AIG General Insurance Company Limited (UIN: IRDAN108RP0001V02201112). It outlines the contract basis, stating that the proposal, premium, and documents accepted by both parties form the contract, with payment subject to terms, conditions, and proof of compensation. It provides 35 definitions covering key terms such as Backup data source/Weather Station, Bank, Beneficiary, Company, Day/Daily, Data Provider, Reference Data Source/Weather Station, Deductible, Endorsement, Exclusions, Exit, Franchise, Policy, Policy Schedule/Certificate of Insurance, Insured/Policyholder, Missing weather data, Notional Rate, Observed Weather Index, Payout, Policy Period/Period of Insurance, Proposal Form, Rainfall, Relative Humidity, Strike, Sum Insured, Sunshine Hours, Temperature, Unit, Weather Index Risk Period, Weather Index Phase Period, Weather Parameter Benchmark, Weather Index (including parameters like Rainfall, Temperature, Humidity, Fog, Wind Speed, Hailstorm, Sunshine hours, Cyclone, Pressure, Inundation/Flood, and other proxy parameters such as solar irradiation, air pollution, soil moisture, and satellite-based indices NDVI, NDWI, Evapotranspiration index), We/us/our, Windspeed, and You/your/yourself. Finally, it describes the Scope of Cover, where the Company agrees to compensate the Insured for deviation of the Observed Weather Index from the Strike within a specific geographical location and Policy period/Weather Index Risk Period/Weather Index Phase Period, subject to the maximum Sum Insured as specified in the Schedule.

title: 2. SCOPE OF COVER:
summary: The text defines key terms for a Weather Insurance Policy, including 'Sunshine Hours', 'Temperature', 'Unit', 'Weather Index Risk Period', 'Weather Index Phase Period', 'Weather Parameter Benchmark', 'Weather Index' with its parameters (e.g., Rainfall, Temperature, Humidity, Fog, Wind Speed, Hailstorm, Sunshine hours, Cyclone, Pressure, Inundation/Flood, and proxy parameters like solar irradiation, air pollution, soil moisture, and satellite indices), 'We/us/our', 'Windspeed', and 'You/your/yourself'. It outlines the Scope of Cover, agreeing to compensate the insured for deviations in the Observed Weather Index from the Strike, subject to terms, conditions, exclusions, location, policy period, and Sum Insured. It also includes Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited's contact and registration details.

title: 3. EXCLUSIONS
summary: The text outlines exclusions (nuclear, non-weather-related, terrorism, war, pandemic, force majeure), basis of claim assessment (payment conditions based on weather index deviation and certified data), and claim procedure (automatic settlement, information requirements, company rights).

summary: The text outlines key provisions of a Weather Insurance Policy, including earthquake exclusion, claim assessment based on Observed Weather Index versus Strike with payment formula and Sum Insured cap, no liability when index conditions are unmet, and settlement using certified data. It details claim procedures such as automatic calculation without claim forms, payment timing, insured's cooperation duties, no communication for no deviation, interim payments, and the company's rights to enter and examine premises with forfeiture for non-compliance. It also covers back-up and fallback data sources with a specific fallback methodology, and general conditions on limitation period, legal ownership, and agreed bank clause.

title: 6. GENERAL CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO THE POLICY:

nodes.title: Weather Insurance Policy: Fallback Data, General Conditions, and Legal Provisions
nodes.summary: The page outlines policy conditions regarding the insured's duty to assist and comply, forfeiture of benefits for non-compliance, and procedures for using back-up or fallback weather data when primary data is unavailable, including a detailed fallback methodology for missing data. It also covers general conditions: limitation period for claims due to weather index deviation, legal ownership requiring proof of insurable interest, and the Agreed Bank Clause for payment of policy monies.

nodes.title: 6.3 Agreed Bank Clause:
nodes.summary: The text outlines provisions for forfeiture of benefits if the insured fails to comply or obstructs the company. It details the use of backup data sources and a fallback methodology for missing weather data, involving replacement with historical averages. It then lists general conditions including limitation period, legal ownership requirements, agreed bank clause for payments and notices, incontestability and duty of disclosure, dispute resolution via Indian courts, and an arbitration clause for quantum disputes under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

nodes.title: Policy Payment, Disclosure, Disputes, and Arbitration Clauses
key_items: 6.4 Incontestability and Duty of Disclosure: The Policy shall be null
nodes.summary: The page covers policy provisions on Bank receipts discharging the Company and binding all insured parties, notices to the Bank being sufficient with a copy to the insured, Bank actions on adjustments or arbitration binding all parties without impairing the Bank's recovery rights, policy nullity for untrue statements or fraud, Indian court jurisdiction for disputes on interpretation and terms, and arbitration procedures for quantum disputes under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as amended in 2015, excluding cases where liability is disputed.

nodes.title: 6.6 Arbitration clause:
nodes.summary: The text covers policy provisions on bank receipts discharging the company, notices to the bank, bank settlements binding on insured parties, incontestability and duty of disclosure rendering the policy void for misstatements or fraud, dispute resolution through Indian courts, arbitration for quantum disputes under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, cancellation conditions with refund rules based on a short period rate table, and customer service grievance procedures including contact details and response timelines.

nodes.title: Policy Cancellation, Refund Terms, and Grievance Procedure
nodes.summary: The page covers the condition precedent for legal action requiring an arbitrator's award, the cancellation clause (6.7) detailing company cancellation for misrepresentation, fraud, or non-disclosure with 15 days' notice and no refund, cancellation for non-cooperation or by insured with premium computed per short period rate table if no claim occurred, and no refund if any claim is admitted or lodged. It includes a refund table based on policy duration. It also covers customer service and grievance procedure (6.8) with 24/7 helpline, email, postal address, servicing branch, Nodal Officer contact via website, 10-day response time with interim reply if longer, and company contact information including registered office, toll-free numbers, email, website, IRDA registration, and CIN.

nodes.title: Weather Insurance Policy Escalation and Ombudsman Details
nodes.summary: The page outlines escalation procedures for a Weather Insurance Policy, detailing Level 1 and Level 2 contacts with response timelines, and provides information on approaching the Insurance Ombudsman if grievances remain unresolved. It includes specific Ombudsman office details for Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, and Bhubaneshwar, along with Tata AIG's corporate contact information and registration numbers.
